newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket to launch new INTELSAT satellite.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket to launch new INTELSAT satellite.

text.p: Western Europe's 94th Ariane rocket is scheduled to blast off from French Guiana on Thursday carrying the first in a new series of satellites for INTELSAT, space officials said on Wednesday.
The Washington-based International Telecommunications Satellite Organisation (INTELSAT) said its INTELSAT 801 satellite will provide voice, data and video services to the Indian Ocean region.
An Ariane 44P rocket equipped with four solid strap-on boosters is scheduled to lift the 3.4 tonne satellite into space. It was built by Lockheed Martin Corp Martin Astro Space in New Jersey.
The launch is set for between 9.16 p.m. and 10.10 p.m. (0016 and 0110 GMT Friday) from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.

The Paris-based Arianespace company that launches the Ariane-4 rocket series leads the commercial satellite launch market and has successfully placed 17 heavy satellites into orbit aboard 11 Ariane rockets since January 1996.
The company said it has firm orders to launch 40 satellites worth an estimated $3.4 billion.
